# .github/

This repository's own continuous integration and the instruction files its review bots read. Nothing here is catalog content.

- `copilot-instructions.md`, `instructions/code-review.md` and `instructions/*.instructions.md` are rendered by the bot-instructions package and each names its generator in a comment: line 1 of the first two, and below the `applyTo` frontmatter in an `instructions/*.instructions.md`. Change `[bot-instructions]` in the effective manifest and re-render, never the file.
- `instructions/code-review.md` is this repository's whole review doctrine. `AGENTS.md` § Code Review Rules is the directive line that sends Codex there, and `copilot-instructions.md` carries the same pointer for Copilot.
- Every job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner. This repository is public and declares no self-hosted runner; the two publish workflows read `vars.CI_RUNNER_2V` for the fleet's runner and fall back to `ubuntu-latest`, which is what runs here since the variable is unset.
- `own-catalog.yml` holds this repository to the same check a consumer gets by calling `catalog-check.yml`, which is the reusable workflow consumers call; keep the caller's content out of the reusable one.
- `skill-tests.yml` is the suite runner [`../skills/AGENTS.md`](../skills/AGENTS.md) names; it carries the `tools/` and `hooks/` suites and the Bash 3.2 legs as well. Its `changes` job reads the change class once through `actions/change-class`, and [`../tools/ci-job-set`](../tools/ci-job-set) turns that class, the changed paths and the event into the lane selection every gated job reads, in its own condition or, for the shell shards, in the shard matrix. A merge group whose tree the pull request's passing run already tested is handed that run's record as `proof_record`, and `ci-job-set` stands down what that run ran, so such a group runs the macOS legs the pull request did not run. The aggregators keep the required contexts present through [`../tools/ci-aggregate`](../tools/ci-aggregate), which accepts a skipped lane only where the selection authorized it. The `CI` job is the one every other job reports into, the three aggregators excepted, and the context the organization ruleset of [`../docs/decisions/D003-one-merge-path.md`](../docs/decisions/D003-one-merge-path.md) requires beside `Review gate`. It holds every lane the `Skill suites (shell + node)`, `Cargo (workspace tests)` and `macOS cargo (workspace tests)` aggregators hold, plus `gate-selftest`, Preflight and Markdown. The `Preflight (diff-scoped deterministic checks)` and `Markdown (format + references)` jobs run on pull requests alone, and `CI` accepts their skip on a merge group against that same event condition. The doc-limits and todo-ban steps of `Bot instructions` run on pull requests alone too: a byte ceiling and a work marker are budgets the pull request answers for, and a merge group is ejected only for a defect, so the bot-instructions check beside them and review-gate's `validate.sh` run on both events.
- `actions/change-class` is the composite action this repository's workflows read a change class from, and the one a consumer references as `vanillagreencom/kendex/.github/actions/change-class@main` in place of calling its vendored classifier, per [`../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md`](../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md) § Through the composite action. It wraps [`../skills/harness-ci/scripts/change-class`](../skills/harness-ci/scripts/change-class) and `harness-only --mode docs` and classifies nothing itself; it decides `lanes` from those two verdicts, and each lane's verdict from `lanes` and the paths a consumer's default-branch `.github/ci-lanes.conf` declares. `actions/change-class/proof` beside it asks GitHub, with the job token and `actions: read`, whether a passing run of the same workflow already tested the same tree, per [`../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md`](../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md) § Proof reuse; the action stands down what that run's record covers of the lanes the workflow says do the same work on every event, publishes the record as `proof_record`, and uploads this run's own record for the run after it. Its suites are [`../tools/tests/change-class-action.test.sh`](../tools/tests/change-class-action.test.sh) and [`../tools/tests/change-class-proof.test.sh`](../tools/tests/change-class-proof.test.sh). Its `classifier` input names the checkout the shipped scripts are read from, and `skill-tests.yml` passes a separate default-branch checkout, so the classifier and the orch contract it measures by are never the pull request's copies. The wrapper itself, `tools/ci-job-set`, `tools/ci-aggregate` and `tools/rust-reads` do run from the pull request's tree: review holds them, and `tools/ci-job-set` runs every lane for a change to any of them. A change to the classifier is proved by the harness-ci suite.
- `lock-record.yml` runs [`../tools/lock-record`](../tools/lock-record) on every push to `main` with a kendex built from that tree: it re-records `.kendex-lock.json` where a merge moved it and lands the record through the rolling pull request `kendex/lock`, armed with the lanes app's token from the `kendex` environment. The choice is [`../docs/decisions/D007-lock-record-on-main.md`](../docs/decisions/D007-lock-record-on-main.md); the script's suite is [`../crates/cli/tests/lock_record.rs`](../crates/cli/tests/lock_record.rs).
- `review-gate-writer.yml` is a relay whose body must equal the review-gate package's template, which [`../skills/review-gate/scripts/validate-workflow.sh`](../skills/review-gate/scripts/validate-workflow.sh) checks.
- `release.yml` is [`../docs/RELEASING.md`](../docs/RELEASING.md).
- `publish-aur.yml` and `publish-homebrew.yml` carry `packaging/` to the AUR and the Homebrew tap; triggers, the dry-run dispatch and the secrets each needs are [`../packaging/README.md`](../packaging/README.md) § Publishing. Neither is called by `release.yml`: a release is published as a draft and the recipe bump follows it.
